title: Implementing Security on AWS using AWS Config and IAM
objectives: Understand the importance of configuration management in cloud security
Configure AWS Config to monitor and report changes to AWS resources
Use IAM roles to grant permissions for AWS Config
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of AWS services and security best practices

mission_brief.briefing: As a Cloud Security Operations Specialist, you are responsible for implementing security controls on AWS. Your mission is to configure AWS Config and IAM roles to ensure compliance with our company's security policies.
rules_of_engagement: Do not introduce any unnecessary changes to the system or environment
Follow all instructions provided by your instructor
Complete the lab within the allocated time

content.concept:
AWS Config is a service that helps you assess, audit, and evaluate your AWS resource configurations and inventory. It allows you to monitor and report changes to your resources, ensuring compliance with your organization's security policies.

Expansion: Explain the security rationale, the operational risk if this is misconfigured, and how an operator verifies correctness under pressure.
content.walkthrough: To configure AWS Config, navigate to the AWS Management Console and search for 'Config'. From there, select 'Settings' and then 'Organization Settings'. Ensure that 'Configuration recorder' is enabled. Next, create an IAM role for AWS Config, attaching the necessary permissions to monitor resources.
checkpoints: Check if AWS Config is enabled in your account
Verify that the correct IAM role is attached to AWS Config
Monitor resource changes using AWS Config
common_mistakes: Failing to enable AWS Config or configure it correctly
Incorrectly assigning permissions to the IAM role for AWS Config
Not regularly monitoring and reviewing resource changes with AWS Config

lab.setup: Create an AWS account (if not already existing) and ensure that you have necessary permissions.
steps: Enable AWS Config in your account using the command `aws configservice get-configuration-recorder-status --configuration-recorder-name 'MyConfigRecorder'`
Create an IAM role for AWS Config using the command `aws iam create-role --role-name 'AWSServiceRoleForConfig'`

Attach necessary permissions to the IAM role for AWS Config using the command `aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name 'AWSServiceRoleForConfig' --policy-arn 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSServiceRoleForConfig'`
Monitor resource changes using AWS Config by running the command `aws configservice get-resource-configurations --configuration-recorder-name 'MyConfigRecorder'`
Validate the configuration by checking the AWS Config dashboard
safety: Ensure you have necessary permissions and follow all instructions provided by your instructor
Do not introduce any unnecessary changes to the system or environment
Regularly review and monitor resource changes with AWS Config
